Title: The Ultimate Reverse-Seared Cowboy Ribeye
Protein Cut: Thick-cut bone-in Ribeye or Tomahawk (1.5 to 2 inches thick)
Cook Method: Low-Oven Slow Roast & Cast-Iron Reverse Sear
Ingredients: 1 bone-in cowboy ribeye steak (approx 2 lbs, 1.75 to 2 inches thick) | 1.5 tbsp coarse kosher salt | 1 tbsp freshly cracked black peppercorns | 1 tbsp high-smoke avocado oil | 2 tbsp unsalted butter | 2 sprigs fresh rosemary
Instructions: 1. Season steak heavily with coarse kosher salt and pepper on all sides. Place on wire rack set in rimmed baking sheet; let sit 30 minutes at room temperature (or chill uncovered overnight to dry surface). 2. Preheat oven to 250°F (120°C). 3. Transfer steak on wire rack to oven. Bake slowly for 35 to 45 minutes until internal thermometer inserted into center registers 110°F for rare, 120°F for medium-rare, or 130°F for medium. 4. Remove steak from oven. Heat cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot; add avocado oil. 5. Sear steak for 45 to 90 seconds per side to form deep mahogany crust. Add butter and rosemary in last 30 seconds, spooning butter over top. 6. Rest on warm plate 5 minutes before slicing.
Source: How To Reverse Sear A Steak: Step-by-Step Recipe - Allen Brothers (Section: Method & Temperature Guide)
Notes: CRITICAL TEMPERATURE DISAGREEMENT: Allen Brothers explicitly directs pulling thick steak from 250°F oven at 120°F for medium-rare (or 110°F for rare / 130°F for medium) because the high-heat cast-iron sear and subsequent rest adds 10°F-15°F of carryover heat, finishing at 130°F-135°F. This deliberately conflicts with the flat FDA recommendation of 145°F, which culinary experts note results in overcooked, medium-well steak.

Title: Grilled T-Bone Steak with Herb Seasoning
Ingredients: 1 T-Bone steak (approx 16 oz, 1-inch thick) | 1 tbsp olive oil | 1 tsp coarse salt | 1 tsp cracked black pepper | 1/2 tsp garlic powder | 1/2 tsp dried thyme
Instructions: 1. Pat T-bone steak thoroughly dry. Combine salt, pepper, garlic powder, and thyme; rub all over steak with olive oil. 2. Preheat grill to medium-high direct heat. 3. Place steak directly over heat; grill 4 to 5 minutes on first side until grill marks form. 4. Flip and grill 4 to 5 minutes on second side. 5. Check temperature: remove at 135°F for medium-rare or 150°F for medium. 6. Stand covered on plate for 5 minutes to allow juices to settle and carryover heat to finish cooking to 145°F (medium-rare) or 160°F (medium).
Source: BEEF COOKERY - NDBeef (Section: Grilling Steaks, Page 6)
Notes: Temperature & resting protocol: NDBeef defines medium-rare doneness as 145°F and medium as 160°F. Instructions state to remove steak from grill 10°F below target (135°F for med-rare, 150°F for medium) and allow a 5-minute standing rest to reach final temperature.

Title: Cast-Iron Seared Flat Iron Steak with Garlic Butter
Ingredients: 1.5 lbs flat iron steak | 1 tbsp neutral cooking oil | 2 tbsp unsalted butter | 3 cloves garlic, smashed | 2 sprigs fresh thyme | 1 tsp kosher salt | 1/2 tsp cracked black pepper
Instructions: 1. Pat flat iron steak dry and season generously with kosher salt and pepper. 2. Heat oil in heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering. 3. Lay steak in pan; sear undisturbed for 4 minutes until dark caramelized crust forms. 4. Flip steak, immediately drop butter, smashed garlic, and thyme into pan. 5. Baste steak continuously with melted herb butter for 3-4 minutes until internal temperature reads 135°F-140°F. 6. Transfer to board and rest 5 minutes; slice thinly across the grain.
Source: BEEF COOKERY - NDBeef (Section: Skillet Cookery & Flat Iron Steaks, Page 8)
Notes: Cut characteristics: Flat iron is the second most tender beef cut after tenderloin; source stresses searing over high heat to medium-rare (pull at 135°F-140°F) and resting 5 minutes. Overcooking past medium toughens this cut.

Title: Grilled Ribeye with Ancho Chili Bourbon Butter
Cook Method: Direct Flame Grilling & Compound Butter Baste
Ingredients: 2 boneless ribeye steaks (12 oz each) | 1 tbsp olive oil | 1.5 tsp coarse kosher salt | 1 tsp black pepper | Compound Butter: 4 tbsp unsalted butter (softened), 1 tsp ancho chili powder, 1 tsp Kentucky bourbon, 1 clove minced garlic, 1 tsp chopped fresh chives
Instructions: 1. Mash softened butter with ancho chili powder, bourbon, minced garlic, chives, and pinch of salt; roll into log in plastic wrap and chill. 2. Bring steaks to room temperature for 20 minutes; rub with olive oil, salt, and pepper. 3. Preheat charcoal or gas grill to high direct heat (450°F-500°F). 4. Place ribeyes over direct flames; grill 4-5 minutes per side, rotating 90 degrees halfway through for crosshatch sear marks. 5. Pull steaks at 130°F-135°F for medium-rare. 6. Immediately top each hot steak with a thick slice of ancho chili bourbon butter; let rest 5 minutes while butter melts into meat.
Source: Masterchef PDF - Bookey (Section: Masterchef Mystery Box Steak Specialties)
Notes: Fat marbling & temperature: Ribeye steaks require high heat to render intramuscular fat cap; source pulls at 130°F-135°F for medium-rare, letting compound butter melt during the mandatory 5-minute rest.

Title: Pan-Seared T-Bone with Peach-Tarragon Reduction
Ingredients: 1 large T-Bone steak (18 oz) | 1 tbsp grapeseed oil | 1 tbsp butter | 1 ripe peach, diced | 1 shallot, minced | 1/4 cup dry white wine | 1 tbsp fresh tarragon, chopped | 1 tsp kosher salt | 1/2 tsp pepper
Instructions: 1. Season T-bone generously with kosher salt and black pepper. 2. Heat grapeseed oil in large skillet over high heat. Sear steak 4 minutes per side until rich crust develops. 3. Add 1 tbsp butter, baste 1 minute, and remove steak to warm platter to rest (pull at 135°F for med-rare). 4. In same skillet, add minced shallot and diced peach; cook 2 minutes. 5. Deglaze skillet with white wine, simmering 2 minutes while scraping pan fond. Stir in chopped tarragon. 6. Spoon warm peach-tarragon pan sauce over rested steak.
Source: Masterchef PDF - Bookey (Section: Fine Dining Steak Creations)
Notes: Cooking precision: Dual-muscle cooking (strip and tenderloin on bone) requires pulling at 135°F to prevent the smaller tenderloin portion from drying out while the strip develops full crust.

Title: Filet Mignon Three Ways (Oven-Finished Tenderloin)
Protein Cut: Center-cut beef tenderloin filet mignon (2 inches thick)
Ingredients: 2 center-cut filet mignon steaks (8 oz each, 2 inches thick) | 1 tbsp clarified butter or olive oil | 1.5 tsp coarse sea salt | 1 tsp cracked black pepper | 2 cloves garlic, crushed | 2 sprigs fresh thyme
Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F (204°C). 2. Tie filets with butcher's twine for uniform thickness; season generously with coarse salt and cracked pepper. 3. Heat clarified butter in ovenproof stainless or cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking. 4. Sear filets 2 minutes per side and 1 minute on rounded edges until evenly browned. 5. Top each filet with crushed garlic clove and thyme sprig; transfer skillet directly to 400°F oven. 6. Bake 4 to 6 minutes until internal temperature registers 125°F-130°F (rare) or 130°F-135°F (medium-rare). 7. Transfer to cutting board and rest 5 minutes before serving.
Source: Masterchef PDF - Bookey (Section: Filets Three Ways Masterclass)
Notes: Technique guidelines: Extremely lean tenderloin cut requires high-heat searing followed by short 400°F oven finish (4-6 min). Source pulls at 130°F-135°F for medium-rare; warns against cooking past 140°F due to lack of intramuscular marbling.

Title: Quick-Broiled Top Sirloin Steak
Ingredients: 2 top sirloin steaks (approx 8 oz each, 3/4-inch thick) | 1 tbsp melted butter or olive oil | 1 tsp steak seasoning or salt and pepper
Instructions: 1. Preheat oven broiler on HIGH. Position broiler pan 3 to 4 inches below heating element. 2. Brush steaks lightly with melted butter or oil; sprinkle evenly with seasoning. 3. Place steaks on unheated rack of broiler pan. 4. Broil for 3 minutes. Carefully flip steaks with tongs. 5. Broil second side for 3 minutes (total 6 minutes for 3/4-inch steak). 6. Remove when internal thermometer reaches 145°F. Rest 3 minutes before slicing.
Source: Ultimate Guide to Beef | Burgers' Smokehouse (Section: How to Cook Beef - Broiling)
Notes: Timing & thickness: Burgers' Smokehouse broiling chart specifies exact timing of 3 minutes per side (6 minutes total) for 3/4-inch sirloin to achieve 145°F internal temperature, followed by a mandatory 3-minute rest.

Title: Marinated Skirt Steak (Carne Asada Style)
Protein Cut: Beef skirt steak or flank steak
Ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef skirt steak, trimmed | 1/3 cup fresh orange juice | 2 tbsp fresh lime juice | 2 tbsp soy sauce | 3 cloves garlic, minced | 1 tsp ground cumin | 1/2 tsp chili powder | 1 tbsp olive oil
Instructions: 1. Whisk orange juice, lime juice, soy sauce, garlic, cumin, chili powder, and olive oil in shallow glass dish. 2. Add skirt steak, turning to coat; marinate 30 minutes at room temperature (or up to 4 hours refrigerated). 3. Preheat grill to maximum high heat (500°F). 4. Remove steak from marinade, shaking off excess liquid. 5. Grill directly over intense heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred on exterior and medium-rare inside (130°F-135°F). 6. Rest 5 minutes on cutting board; slice thinly across the grain at a 45-degree angle.
Source: How to Cook Beef: Best Cooking Method for Every Cut - Clover Meadows Beef (Section: Flank & Skirt Steak Stir-Frying & Grilling)
Notes: Grain slicing rule: Thin muscle cut cooked rapidly over intense direct heat (2-3 min/side) to avoid moisture loss. Critical instruction: must be sliced thinly against the grain to break up tough long fibers.
